input.quote: 16.2 Indemnification of Ono. Array shall indemnify and hold harmless each of Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees and the directors, officers and employees of Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees and the successors and assigns of any of the foregoing (the "Ono Indemnitees"), from and against any and all Liabilities from any Third Party Claims incurred by any Ono Indemnitee, arising from, or occurring as a result of:
input.rationale: Array does give a two-way indemnity (Section 16.2) covering its own Array Territory commercialization, its own clinical studies and its breach of the Article 15 representations, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure in 16.3 and fault-based allocation in 16.4 — so this is not a one-way Ono indemnity. However, the indemnity omits the material term this rule turns on: there is no Array indemnity for Third Party claims that the licensed Products (i.e., Array's own compounds, patents and know-how) infringe or misappropriate Third Party IP, and Section 11.4(a) affirmatively puts the defence of such "Infringement Actions" on the Subject Party "at its own expense", leaving Ono to fund infringement claims on technology Array licensed to us. The Article 15 IP reps are knowledge-qualified and given only as of the Effective Date, so they do not close the gap. Because the fallback expressly requires a licensor/vendor IP indemnity (with usual exclusions), the clause fails the fallback on IP infringement and is a deviation. Redline adds a new Section 16.2(e) IP indemnity with the customary modification and combination carve-outs, preserving the existing gross negligence/willful misconduct exception; the absence of a general Array gross negligence/willful misconduct limb is noted but not separately flagged.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an Array indemnity for Third Party claims that the licensed Products infringe Third Party intellectual property rights, with the usual modification and combination carve-outs, because our playbook requires the licensor to stand behind IP infringement claims arising from the rights it licenses to us. As drafted, Section 16.2 covers only Array's own activities and Article 15 breaches, while Section 11.4 leaves us bearing our own defence costs for infringement claims on Array's technology.
proposal.summary: Add third-party IP infringement indemnity from Array to Ono in Section 16.2 with standard modification/combination exclusions.
